audit_findings.title: Pre-acquisition owner earnings are paired with post-acquisition financing
audit_findings.magnitude: Transaction consideration was $163.863m; cash fell $114.664m and debt rose $56.994m from 2025-12-31 to 2026-06-30; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes Petersen earnings and acquisition-financing interest, while the bridge includes the post-acquisition cash balance but does not deduct debt.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition price was $ 166.5 million plus customary working capital adjustments and was funded through the Company’s cash and its Revolver Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch involving an acquisition equal to 14.2% of the $1,148.703m year-end equity base. Omitting Petersen earnings understates value, while omitting the associated interest burden or debt claim overstates value. The net direction cannot be established, but the transaction scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the valuation on one date and perimeter using post-acquisition trailing owner earnings, or a documented Petersen pro forma including target owner earnings, incremental after-tax interest, integration costs and the corresponding cash/debt bridge.

audit_findings.title: Petersen’s assumed liabilities remain unverified
audit_findings.magnitude: The preliminary purchase-price allocation reports $7.347m of other liabilities assumed; any subsequent adjustment or omitted claim is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Assumed operating obligations can reduce future OE, while debt-like, contingent or tax claims may require an equity-bridge deduction if not already captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Because the valuation procedures are ongoing, the Company is unable to provide the initial allocation of the purchase price at this time.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q partially resolves the finding by reporting $7.347m of other liabilities assumed, so no additional omitted liability is demonstrated. The allocation remains preliminary, however, and the record does not disaggregate those liabilities or establish whether further working-capital, lease, tax or contingent claims exist. Their potential value effect therefore cannot be classified as material from the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the finalized purchase-price allocation and reconcile every assumed liability, working-capital adjustment and contingent payment to the June balance sheet; rerun only for items not already captured in normalized OE or the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The after-interest DCF does not address the 2027 financing reset
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 interest expense increased $2.538m year over year; a 200 bp rate change at current variable-rate borrowings changes quarterly interest expense by approximately $1.3m; long-run value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because OE is measured after interest, acquisition borrowing and future variable-rate financing costs must reduce forecast OE rather than be handled solely as debt context.
audit_findings.evidence: The notional principal is scheduled to adjust each quarter to match the amortization of the Term Facility up to the swap termination date of August 31, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The precise 2027 premise is no longer established: the May 2026 credit agreement now matures in 2031, and the latest filing describes the debt as variable-rate. The underlying error remains demonstrated because the $115.2m FY2025 anchor predates Petersen financing, while H1 2026 interest expense already increased $2.538m. The filed $1.3m quarterly sensitivity is large enough relative to the bull case’s $6.02-per-share premium over market to be reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine current hedge coverage and effective rates under the 2026 facility, normalize the post-Petersen after-tax interest burden through 2031 and beyond, and rerun OE without double-counting the perimeter correction in finding 1.

audit_findings.title: The gross cash add-back may not all be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $194.995m is added to equity value, equal to $15.83 per diluted share and 10.2% of base equity value; $133.8m was held by foreign subsidiaries; the unavailable portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating cash requirement, repatriation tax or access restriction reduces the cash bridge added dollar-for-dollar to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company had $174.5 million in cash and cash equivalents held by its foreign subsidiaries as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably treats all cash as distributable surplus, although 68.6% was held by foreign subsidiaries and the filing says repatriated funds may be used for debt, working capital, investments and acquisitions. The add-back exceeds the approximately $74.2m total bull-case premium over the market price; therefore, a cash haircut of about 38% would eliminate that premium. The record does not establish the proper haircut, but the exposure is materially large.
audit_findings.action: Classify June 2026 cash by jurisdiction, legal availability and minimum operating need; estimate applicable withholding or other leakage and rerun the bridge using only net demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains potentially nonrecurring transition charges
audit_findings.mechanism: Demonstrably nonrecurring charges embedded in FY2025 OE depress the $115.2m anchor and every forecast year grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income was impacted by the CEO transition costs, acquisition and integration expenses, and ongoing restructuring efforts.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that CEO transition, acquisition, integration and restructuring costs affected FY2025 income, but it does not quantify the FY2025 components or establish which costs will not recur. Consequently, an understatement of normalized OE is possible but neither its amount nor its ability to change the valuation conclusion can be established. The separately disclosed $4.3m of second-quarter 2026 costs does not quantify the FY2025 adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 charge-level reconciliation, tax-effect each item, remove only costs demonstrably nonrecurring, retain a normalized recurring integration and restructuring burden, and rerun all scenarios from the revised anchor.
